description.purpose: Deterministic ODCS v3.2.0 DataContract for spicy-regs publication family 'bill-family' (20 table(s)), targeting DDK domain 'spicycongress'.
description.usage: Verify Parquet Arrow schema parity before publishing or consuming generations.

schema.name: bill_actions
schema.description: One row per entry of the bill's own action list, in publisher order. Committee, calendar and roll call references appear under the action that states them. Amendment actions have a separate scope. API rows carry the exact page digest, observation time and zero-based page position. Each row also carries the stage the action text implies.

properties.name: bill_id
properties.description: The bill this action belongs to.

properties.name: action_index
properties.description: Zero-based position in the publisher's own action list, which runs newest first: 0 is the bill's latest action. Part of the identity.

properties.name: action_date
properties.description: The publisher's actionDate for this action.

properties.name: action_time
properties.description: The publisher's actionTime, where the source system states one.

properties.name: action_text
properties.description: The action text exactly as written, whitespace included; NULL when the publisher stated none.

properties.name: action_code
properties.description: The publisher's action code, which is what the became-law rule keys on.

authoritativeDefinitions.description: billstatus-xml-user-guide-2026-08-03.md section 3, Action Code Element Possible Values (lines 449-497)

properties.name: action_type
properties.description: The publisher's action type (IntroReferral, Floor, BecameLaw...).

authoritativeDefinitions.description: billstatus-xml-user-guide-2026-08-03.md section 4, Actions Type Element Possible Values (lines 498-532)

properties.name: source_system_name
properties.description: Name of the system that reported the action.

properties.name: recorded_vote_count
properties.description: How many recordedVote entries this action carries.

properties.name: is_latest_action
properties.description: True on the one actions[] entry the publisher's separate latestAction element names.

properties.name: stage
properties.description: The stage this one action's qualified code and text classify as, in the same vocabulary as congress_bills.stage (`introduced`, `committee`, `calendared`, `passed_chamber`, `other_chamber`, `conference`, `cleared`, `presented`, `law`, or the outcomes `failed` and `vetoed`; never `passed_both`, which is a bill's state, not one action's); `introduced` with stage_rule NULL when no rule classifies the action, as for the desk or a floor step in the bill's own chamber. An action reads `cleared` where its own words complete agreement on one text; a chamber's agreement to a conference report reads `conference` here, and the bill reads `cleared` from the second, or from its listed enrolled text, which no action reads. One action's classification, not the bill's state.

properties.name: action_committees
properties.description: Ordered committee references stated on this action. NULL means the source omitted the group. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.

properties.name: action_calendar_numbers
properties.description: Calendar references stated on this action, without inheriting bill-level calendars. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.

properties.name: action_recorded_votes

customProperties.value: STRUCT(chamber VARCHAR, congress VARCHAR, date VARCHAR, full_action_name VARCHAR, roll_number VARCHAR, session_number VARCHAR, url VARCHAR)[]

properties.description: Ordered recorded-vote references the publisher attached to this action. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.

properties.name: source_page_sha256
properties.description: Exact Congress.gov API child-page digest, when the action came from that route.

properties.name: source_page_observed_at
properties.description: When the child page was captured, independent of the parent observation and action date.

properties.name: source_page_row_index
properties.description: Zero-based position of the action in its retained API page.

schema.dataGranularityDescription: One row per entry of the bill's own action list, in publisher order; actions recorded under the bill's amendments (amendments/amendment/actions) are not rows, so a roll call on an amendment can have no action here.

schema.name: bill_committee_activities
schema.description: One committee or subcommittee activity a bill's BILLSTATUS document lists: the committee, the activity's name and timestamp as written, and an occurrence number for exact repeats. Not a complete record of what committees did: a report can appear in `bill_actions` only (119-s-545 lists Markup By and no Reported By). A re-read merges on the key and keeps the newer document's row, so an activity the publisher later drops is not removed.

properties.name: bill_id
properties.description: The bill whose committee this activity belongs to.

properties.name: system_code
properties.description: The publisher's identifier of the committee or subcommittee that did it (ssju00).

properties.name: activity_name
properties.description: The publisher's activity name exactly as written, in either capitalisation it uses (Reported By and Reported by, Referred To and Referred to): Referred To, Markup By, Reported By, Discharged From, Hearings By (full committee), Hearings By (subcommittee), Reported Original Measure, Bills of Interest - Exchange of Letters, Unknown.

properties.name: activity_date
properties.description: The publisher's timestamp for it, as written (2026-05-11T20:30:49Z), in UTC: an evening step can fall on the next day here while bill_actions.action_date keeps the day the publisher states for the action (119-hr-1703's discharge: 2026-10-01T03:17:50Z here, 2026-09-30 there). Empty where the item states none, as every Bills of Interest - Exchange of Letters item does.

properties.name: occurrence
properties.description: 1 for an activity's first listing under this committee, 2 for an exact repeat (same name and timestamp), and so on: the publisher lists some referrals twice (119-s-545).

properties.name: parent_system_code
properties.description: The parent committee's system code when the activity is a subcommittee's.

schema.dataGranularityDescription: One row per activity a BILLSTATUS document lists under one of the bill's committees or subcommittees: what the committee did and when. A clean key for a committee's work but not a complete one: 119-s-545's lists Markup By and no Reported By while its actions record the report, so a report can appear in bill_actions only.

customProperties.value: Read from the same committee walk as bill_committees; not yet baselined.
Parent committee of the committee recording activity. Full selected keys and unique parent keys checked on 2026-10-06; CI checks resolution and parent uniqueness.
Committee recording activity on the bill. Full selected keys and unique parent keys checked on 2026-10-06; CI checks resolution and parent uniqueness.
New in spicy-docs 0.54.0: filled as each Congress's BILLSTATUS is re-read; not yet baselined.

schema.name: bill_committees
schema.description: One row per committee or subcommittee named in a bill's BILLSTATUS document. Activities and dates are in `bill_committee_activities`; an action missing from that list may still appear in `bill_actions`. `bill_committee_actions` describes a separate source: House committee activity-report prints.

properties.name: bill_id
properties.description: The bill this referral belongs to.

properties.name: system_code
properties.description: The publisher's own committee identifier (hsap00); what a referral rule keys on.

properties.name: name
properties.description: The committee's name as prose, which no rule reads.

properties.name: chamber
properties.description: The chamber, which the publisher states for a committee and omits for a subcommittee.

properties.name: committee_type
properties.description: The publisher's committee type (Standing, Select...); absent on a subcommittee.

properties.name: parent_system_code
properties.description: The parent committee's system code when this row is a subcommittee.

properties.name: is_subcommittee
properties.description: True when this row came from another committee's subcommittees list.

properties.name: snapshot_update_date
properties.description: The parent document's updateDate, so a committee list is versioned with its bill.

schema.dataGranularityDescription: One row per committee or subcommittee a bill reached, as its BILLSTATUS document names it.

customProperties.value: Complete once committees lists every Congress: the 108th-117th backfill named 78 codes on no 119th list. Measured on a local committee-rosters run over the live children (receipt committee-fixes-2026-09-26/3-rosters-118/runs.json); the published table misses them until it runs.

schema.name: bill_cosponsors
schema.description: One cosponsor occurrence in one retained BILLSTATUS observation, keyed by the bill, the input digest and the list ordinal. A member listed twice keeps two rows; a successfully read absent or empty list replaces the bill's prior rows.

properties.name: bill_id
properties.description: The bill whose source lists the cosponsor.

properties.name: cosponsor_index
properties.description: Zero-based position in the source cosponsors list, including repeated members.

properties.name: bioguide_id
properties.description: Source member identifier; its presence does not prove target resolution.

properties.name: full_name
properties.description: The source's fullName literal.

properties.name: sponsorship_date
properties.description: Literal sponsorshipDate; absent is NULL and present empty is an empty string.

properties.name: is_original
properties.description: Literal isOriginalCosponsor text, without Boolean coercion.

properties.name: sponsorship_withdrawn_date
properties.description: Literal sponsorshipWithdrawnDate; retained BILLSTATUS source observations include positive dates.

properties.name: party
properties.description: Party as the cosponsor entry states it.

properties.name: state
properties.description: State as the cosponsor entry states it.

properties.name: district
properties.description: District as the cosponsor entry states it.

schema.dataGranularityDescription: One cosponsor occurrence in one retained BILLSTATUS observation.

customProperties.value: New source-occurrence output; public population not yet baselined.
Source-listed member identifier; public cosponsor output not yet baselined.

schema.name: bill_family_document_file_outcomes
schema.description: Recorded original producer members and their exact native conversion mappings. Empty partition states have a state witness, without a physical file digest.

properties.name: generation_id
properties.description: Generation that converted the retained producer outputs.

properties.name: source_dataset
properties.description: Original producer dataset whose member was converted.

properties.name: member_ordinal
properties.description: Original member position within the producer dataset.

properties.name: relative_path
properties.description: Original member path relative to its producer dataset; empty partition states have none.

properties.name: partitioned
properties.description: Whether the original producer output was partitioned.

properties.name: row_count
properties.description: Recorded row count in the original producer member or successful empty state.

properties.name: state
properties.description: Converted member, retained processing member, or successful empty partition.

properties.name: original_byte_sha256
properties.description: Exact original physical member byte digest; empty partition states have none.

properties.name: state_witness_sha256
properties.description: Digest of the recorded empty-state witness; this is not a physical file-byte digest.

properties.name: source_schema
properties.description: Original member column names, types, and nullability.

properties.name: source_metadata
properties.description: Original footer metadata as lossless base64 key and value pairs.

properties.name: native_members

customProperties.value: STRUCT(relative_path VARCHAR, sha256 VARCHAR, byte_size BIGINT, row_count BIGINT)[]

properties.description: Exact admitted native member mappings, including relative path, byte digest, size, and row count. Processing-only members have none.

schema.name: bill_publisher_summaries
schema.description: One row per retained CRS summary revision, keyed by bill, summary version, action date and publisher update date. Later update dates preserve earlier rows; repeated copies of the same dated revision merge into one row. `summary_html` is kept exactly as the publisher escaped it. `update_date` preserves the native item clock; legacy `last_summary_update_date` dates the summary itself. `source_schema_version` qualifies those meanings. For `congress-api-v3`, `update_date` is the child response's own updateDate. Read its page digest, capture time and row index from the receipt. A BILLSUM row's `update_date` is a day with no time and its `last_summary_update_date` is NULL. See docs/bill-summary-clocks.md for the schema-qualified query, the BILLSUM rows and replay limits.

properties.name: bill_id
properties.description: The bill this summary describes.

properties.name: summary_version_code
properties.description: The publisher's two-digit summary version code (00 introduced, 53 passed House...).

properties.name: action_date
properties.description: The date of the action this summary describes.

properties.name: action_desc
properties.description: The publisher's description of that action.

properties.name: update_date
properties.description: Literal updateDate of the summary item. In BILLSTATUS 1.0.0 it dates the billSummaries item, not the summary itself; 3.0.0 states it within summary. It does not establish first publication.

properties.name: summary_html
properties.description: The summary exactly as the publisher escaped it, from either placement, untruncated.

properties.name: summary_chars
properties.description: Character length of summary_html, so a truncation upstream is visible without reading it.

properties.name: last_summary_update_date
properties.description: Literal lastSummaryUpdateDate, which dates the summary itself in BILLSTATUS 1.0.0. NULL means absent; empty and malformed source strings remain unchanged. No first-publication claim.

properties.name: source_schema_version
properties.description: The BILLSTATUS version or Congress.gov API format giving the native clock its context.

schema.dataGranularityDescription: One row per retained CRS summary revision, identified by its bill, summary version, action and update date.

schema.name: bill_sections
schema.description: One row per content-bearing node of one bill version, in document order. Published as one file per Congress; the server and the publication readers present them as one table, but a raw download holds one file for each Congress.

properties.name: bill_id
properties.description: The bill this section belongs to.

properties.name: version_code
properties.description: The printing this section was read from.

properties.name: printing_id
properties.description: Which acquisition path supplied the printing; part of the parent version's key.

properties.name: match_path
properties.description: The normalized, division-free cross-version key, unit-separator joined; it can repeat. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.

properties.name: display_path
properties.description: The human-facing path the engine composes, as a Native list. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.

properties.name: element_id
properties.description: The publisher's own id attribute on the element this node came from.

properties.name: section_number
properties.description: The section's own number as displayed (Sec. 1), where it has one.

properties.name: heading
properties.description: The section's header text, empty where the node carries none.

properties.name: body
properties.description: The section's body text, at the grain people actually query.

properties.name: display_text
properties.description: The engine's display rendering of the body, kept apart from the body itself.

properties.name: division_label
properties.description: The division this section sits under, as the engine composes the label.

properties.name: division_key
properties.description: The normalized division key, which is what a cross-version match ignores.

properties.name: body_index
properties.description: Which body element this node came from; a reported bill carries two.

properties.name: seq
properties.description: Position in document order; the section's key within its printing, which the match path cannot be.

properties.name: body_chars
properties.description: Character length of body.

properties.name: version_date
properties.description: The parent printing's date, carried so this table versions with its parent.

properties.name: congress
properties.description: The Congress of the bill, the prefix of bill_id (119 for 119-hr-1), so a host can store the table one file per Congress.

properties.name: body_version_id
properties.description: Stable identity of the substantive captured document body, independent of extraction processing.

schema.dataGranularityDescription: One row per content-bearing node of one bill version, in document order.

customProperties.value: Native subject keys replace source capture keys. The original measured relationship remains in processing_joins; this subject-key relationship has no measured baseline yet.

schema.name: bill_summaries
schema.description: One row per plain-language summary of one printing of a bill. `frame` is stored because without it the summary is not reproducible from the row.

properties.name: bill_id
properties.description: The bill this summary describes.

properties.name: version_code
properties.description: The printing this summary was written from.

properties.name: printing_id
properties.description: Which acquisition path supplied that printing.

properties.name: summary
properties.description: The plain-language paragraph, length-checked before it was stored.

properties.name: audience
properties.description: The short phrase naming the most-affected audience.

properties.name: top_provisions
properties.description: Up to three notable provisions, as a Native list in the model's order. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.

properties.name: money_bill_kind
properties.description: The money-bill kind that selected the framing sentence.

schema.dataGranularityDescription: One row per plain-language summary of one printing of a bill.

customProperties.value: Kept empty by owner decision 34 (fork-delivery-decisions-2026-09-22): the model output that would fill it is not produced; publishes no rows

schema.name: bill_versions
schema.description: One row per printing of a bill, per source that supplied it. The full text is deliberately not a column here: `bill_sections.body` carries it at the grain people query, and the body is re-fetchable by package id and digest.

properties.name: bill_id
properties.description: The bill this printing belongs to.

properties.name: version_code
properties.description: The printing's code: its stage's sealed slug, or a numbered reprint's own package suffix (eas2).

properties.name: printing_id
properties.description: Which acquisition path supplied this row (govinfo, congress, govinfo-pdf, upload).

properties.name: label
properties.description: The publisher's version-type string verbatim, which is not unique per printing.

properties.name: version_date
properties.description: Congress textVersions action-associated date for this printing, not its online publication time; the merge prefers the larger value. An enrolled printing's date is empty at the publisher (BILLSTATUS `<date/>` and the printing's own dc:date), so version_date is '' (not NULL) on enrolled rows, which sorts before every date: order printings with printing_order or NULLIF(version_date, '').

properties.name: package_id
properties.description: The GovInfo BILLS package id, read from a stated format URL rather than derived by name.

properties.name: version_code_is_reprint_ambiguous
properties.description: True when the publisher's version-type string also names a numbered reprint, so the slug alone cannot tell the two printings apart.

properties.name: publisher_stage
properties.description: The root's own bill-stage or resolution-stage attribute: the publisher's word for it.

properties.name: section_count
properties.description: How many content-bearing nodes the flattening produced; the bill_sections row count.

properties.name: equivalent_xml_version_code
properties.description: For a PDF twin, the version_code of the XML row it stands in for.

properties.name: equivalent_printing_id
properties.description: That twin's source.  A version code is not unique across acquisition paths, which is why bill_versions keys on source too, so a twin reference needs both halves to resolve.

properties.name: kind
properties.description: Interpreted document kind: `full_text`, `kind_uncertain` (a full-text slug whose document is too thin to be sure), `procedural_amendments`, `procedural_summary`, or `unknown`.

properties.name: kind_label
properties.description: The display label for this kind, supplied by the caller that owns the vocabulary.

properties.name: kind_warning
properties.description: The inline warning this kind carries, for a version picker.  NULL for `full_text` and for `unknown`, which states none of its own.

properties.name: publication_dates

customProperties.value: STRUCT(field VARCHAR, "value" VARCHAR, state VARCHAR, "precision" VARCHAR, locator VARCHAR, source_sha256 VARCHAR, source_url VARCHAR, observed_at VARCHAR, attributes STRUCT("name" VARCHAR, "value" VARCHAR)[])[]

properties.description: Native SUMMARY/MODS date observations with original values, precision, attributes and exact evidence/capture locators.

properties.name: publication_evidence_status
properties.description: Whether SUMMARY was bracketed or changed; every status leaves the metadata/body version link unverified.

properties.name: body_version_id
properties.description: Stable identity of the substantive captured document body, independent of extraction processing.

schema.dataGranularityDescription: One row per printing of a bill, per source that supplied it.

schema.name: bill_vote_references
schema.description: One row per recorded vote on one bill action: which roll call the bill's own actions say settled it. Read by the `roll-call-votes` rollup to fill `roll_call_votes.bill_id` and its match columns.

properties.name: bill_id
properties.description: The bill whose action carried this entry, keyed as every bill table keys it.

properties.name: chamber
properties.description: The chamber that took the roll call, lowercased (house, senate).

properties.name: congress
properties.description: The numbered Congress the roll call belongs to.

properties.name: session
properties.description: The session number within that Congress, from the entry's sessionNumber.

properties.name: roll_number
properties.description: The roll-call number within that session, from the entry's rollNumber.

properties.name: action_index
properties.description: Position of the action this entry sat on, in the publisher's own newest-first action order at the capture; it rises as actions are added, so it is not a stable key across captures.

properties.name: date
properties.description: The instant the entry states for the vote.

properties.name: full_action_name
properties.description: The guide's seventh field, absent on every entry measured; NULL where the publisher sends none.

customProperties.value: All four fields identify the vote. Congress alone is a filter. Full selected keys and unique parent keys checked on 2026-10-06; CI checks resolution and parent uniqueness.

schema.name: cbo_cost_estimates
schema.description: One row per bill and CBO publication, using build_bill_family's own cbo_cost_estimates output and spicy-docs' feed builder, merged by `merge_cbo_cost_estimates`: where both routes state one bill and publication, the BILLSTATUS row stands. One publication can stand under two bills, and both rows publish.

properties.name: bill_id
properties.description: The bill the source attached this estimate to, as published, keyed the way congress_bills.bill_id is: the bill whose BILLSTATUS record lists it (`billstatus_bulk`), or the bill CBO's feed item names by Bill_Number, by a bare-number Bill_Number and the title's leading citation of that number, or, where Bill_Number is empty, by the citation its title leads with or by the bill the host's laws table says enacted the law it leads with (`cbo_feed`; found_by says which).  Where title_bill_id differs, this number is wrong and title_bill_id names the bill the estimate scores.

properties.name: congress
properties.description: The numbered Congress the bill belongs to.

properties.name: bill_type
properties.description: Lowercase publisher bill or resolution type (hr, s, hjres...).

properties.name: bill_number
properties.description: The measure's number within its Congress and type.

properties.name: publication_id
properties.description: CBO's own publication number, parsed from the stated url by the `cbo_publication_url` rule and part of this row's identity.  This is the key CBO's per-Congress feed also states, so that feed's own spelling of the measure, which no GovInfo route gives, joins here.  It is not unique alone: where the routes file one estimate under two bills, both rows publish -- CBO's feed files 22065, its estimate of P.L. 111-322, under the 112th's H.R. 3082 and the 111th's H.R. 3082 BILLSTATUS lists it -- and title_bill_id names the bill it scores.

properties.name: pub_date
properties.description: The publisher's pubDate for this estimate; the merge prefers the larger value.  It is when CBO published the estimate, not when the bill acted.  A `cbo_feed` row states the feed's Date as the same instant in UTC, spelled as BILLSTATUS spells pubDate.

properties.name: title
properties.description: The estimate's title as the publisher states it, which is usually the bill's own title.

properties.name: description
properties.description: CBO's own statement of which printing it scored ("As ordered reported by the House Committee on Energy and Commerce on March 24, 2023").  The only field that distinguishes two estimates of one bill, and the field that states the stage: 826 of the 118th House's 1,062 rows begin "As ordered reported by the House C", and the tail includes Rules Committee prints, which have no committee report at all.  A `cbo_feed` row's is the feed's Description with the surrounding whitespace this package's feed parser trims, a trailing newline on many.

properties.name: restatements

customProperties.value: STRUCT(estimate_index BIGINT, title VARCHAR, description VARCHAR, pub_date VARCHAR)[]

properties.description: Every other item naming this publication whose fields differ from the row's, in list order, as a Native list of objects carrying `estimate_index` and only the differing fields; `[]` when they agree or there is no other item.  In the 118th (measured 2026-09-20) 9 of the 37 restated rows differ, every one in `title` alone -- CBO re-spelling the bill's title ('Human rights' to 'Human Rights', one double-escaped ampersand).  In the 108th-111th every row carries its http twin, which differs in `url` and, on all but 11 of 4,762, in `description`, which it wraps in a p element.  The column exists so folding onto the identity drops nothing. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.

properties.name: report_citation_count
properties.description: How many committee reports this bill's own BILLSTATUS names, on a `cbo_feed` row too, where the host supplies that record; NULL on a `cbo_feed` row shaped without it. Zero means this document names no report citation; it does not establish that no CRPT package exists. 883 of the 1,368 scored bills of the 118th are nonzero (64.5%), and the Senate shortfall is structural -- 155 of 395 scored Senate bills were reported without a written report.

properties.name: report_citations

customProperties.value: STRUCT(citation VARCHAR, congress VARCHAR, number VARCHAR, part VARCHAR, report_type VARCHAR)[]

properties.description: Every citation that bill's `<committeeReports>` states, as a Native list in publisher order (NULL where report_citation_count is), each carrying the `citation` verbatim and its parsed `congress`, `report_type` and `number` -- the three columns `committee_reports` publishes -- plus `part` where the citation names one.  A part citation has no package id under GovInfo's sealed CRPT grammar, so none is invented; the parsed parts are NULL on any citation outside the measured shape. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.

properties.name: title_bill_id
properties.description: The bill this estimate's own title leads with ("H.R. 3447, a bill to extend ..."), keyed as bill_id is and read by the feed's title rule; for a title leading with a public law ("P.L. 111-322, ..."), the bill the host's laws table says enacted it, where the host supplies that map.  NULL where the title leads with no citation, cites the bill only after its start ("Senate Amendment 1183 to S. 744"), is ambiguous, or names a law the host did not map.  Where it differs from bill_id the row is a numbering error and this is the bill the estimate scores: over the 108th-119th (2026-09-28), 5 BILLSTATUS rows and 5 feed rows by bill titles -- four of CBO's own wrong numbers on both, 112 H.R. 1707 for S. 1707 on the feed, and 114 H.R. 3347 on BILLSTATUS, whose record lists CBO's estimate of H.R. 3447 -- and, with a law map, 2 more on both (P.L. 119-21's estimates filed under H. Con. Res. 14) and 1 more on the feed (P.L. 111-322 filed under the 112th's H.R. 3082, its bill's number in the 111th).  A bill citation reads in the row's own Congress, so this cannot show a link to the same number in another Congress: 115 H.R. 1422's BILLSTATUS lists 52538, CBO's estimate of the 113th's H.R. 1422, and this reads 115-hr-1422; that pub_date, 2013-04-22, precedes the 115th.  On a `cbo_feed` row whose found_by is `title`, `title_law` or `bill_number_title` the title chose bill_id, so the two agree by construction and the agreement proves nothing: 237 of the 108th-119th's feed rows with the host's law map, 235 without (2026-09-28).  title_bill_id_rule names the rule.

schema.dataGranularityDescription: One row per bill and CBO publication a source names as a cost estimate of it: the bill's own BILLSTATUS document or CBO's per-Congress feed, read for every Congress and merged, the bill's own record winning where both name one bill and publication.

customProperties.value: CBO publication identity connects each estimate to its feed observation. A feed publication may name several bills or no bill. Three publication IDs were absent from the selected feed; the cause is not established by this join check. Parent keys were unique in the complete selected inputs checked on 2026-10-03; CI enforces that cardinality.
Bill identified by the title reader; retain its documented extraction caveats. Full selected keys and unique parent keys checked on 2026-10-06; CI checks resolution and parent uniqueness.

schema.name: cbo_estimate_cards
schema.description: One qualified card per CBO publication, with three positional fiscal windows, literal and typed millions, PAYGO and mandate answers, source context and original evidence. Join publication_id to cbo_cost_estimates for source-stated bill links; cards exist independently of whether those bill links resolve.

properties.name: publication_id
properties.description: CBO publication identity, independent of any bill link.

properties.name: congress
properties.description: Congress named by the selected feed.

properties.name: publication_date
properties.description: Selected feed Date as a UTC instant; distinct from archive capture time.

properties.name: publication_title
properties.description: Selected feed Title, including unresolved bill descriptions.

properties.name: publication_context
properties.description: Selected feed Description, retained without inferring bill stage.

properties.name: title
properties.description: Literal card heading.

properties.name: subtitle
properties.description: Literal card subtitle, where printed.

properties.name: unit
properties.description: Normalized fiscal-year amounts in millions of dollars; source_unit keeps the printed unit.

properties.name: source_unit

properties.name: stage
properties.description: The whole bill's interpreted legislative stage: the latest step its actions show under the current rule, not a final outcome. On the ladder: `introduced`, `committee`, `calendared`, `passed_chamber`, `other_chamber`, `passed_both`, `conference`, `cleared`, `presented` or `law` (the terminal rung; the literal is `law`, never `enacted`); or an outcome with no rung, `failed` or `vetoed`. `introduced` is also the default when no rule fires (see stage_rule); NULL where the bill's actions were not examined, which is not a statement about enactment. A number the House reserves for its leadership (title "Reserved for the Speaker.") has no actions: it reads `introduced` with stage_rule NULL, or NULL where GovInfo holds no document. A mention is not an event: taking over the sponsorship of a bill "originally introduced by" another, a floor action citing the text "as introduced" or "as reported", a special rule's report or description, and a star print classify nothing, and where the publisher's action code names a step, the code is read before the text. `calendared` is a placement on the Union, House or Senate Legislative Calendar in the bill's own chamber (a reported bill awaiting the floor, or one placed there unreported under Senate Rule XIV or a discharge); a later report, order to report, subcommittee referral or floor step leaves it `calendared`, and only a referral of the bill to a committee lowers it. `passed_chamber` and `other_chamber` both mean the bill's own chamber has passed it; `other_chamber` adds that the other chamber has received it or taken a calendar, desk or floor step on it. A calendar placement, the desk, a motion to proceed or cloture reads `other_chamber` only where the chamber that took it (as the text names it, else the system that entered it) is not the one the bill's type originates in; in its own chamber the desk, a motion to proceed or cloture moves nothing. `passed_both` means both chambers have passed it (the Library of Congress's 8000 and 17000 where the actions carry codes, else the text) but not, as far as the wording shows, in one text: the second passage carried an amendment the other chamber has not agreed to, or names none either way (the House's "On passage Passed"), and the publisher lists no enrolled text. It is read from the passage that completed it. `conference` is a conference requested, held or reported; the Library of Congress's "Resolving differences" exchange of amendments is not one. `cleared` means both chambers have agreed to one text: the second chamber passed it as it arrived (the Senate "without amendment", or the House on a motion to suspend the rules that names no amendment), a chamber agreed to the other's amendment with no amendment of its own, or both agreed to a conference report; the Library of Congress's "Cleared for White House." (109th-111th Congresses) reads it too. So does a measure both chambers passed in wording that states no agreement (the House's "On agreeing to the resolution Agreed to" on a Senate concurrent resolution) where its BILLSTATUS document lists an enrolled text, GPO's final copy of a measure both chambers passed in identical form. A bill or joint resolution is then ready for the President; a concurrent resolution is complete. `failed` is the latest vote on passage failing in either chamber, a failed two-thirds vote to suspend the rules included: the measure can still pass, and it reads over an earlier passage by the other chamber until a later step. `vetoed` stands until a recorded enactment; a failed override keeps it. The stage never moves back once a chamber has passed the bill: the other chamber's referral or report, a star print or an introduction phrase does not lower it, and only a passage the Senate states it vitiated is undone; where the actions carry publisher codes, the Library of Congress's passage code (8000 House, 17000 Senate) is what holds it. Once `cleared`, no lower rung moves it back. A motion's or a point of order's result ("motion to proceed ... agreed to in Senate") is not the measure's passage, and "disagreed to in Senate" reads `failed`.

properties.name: stage_rule

NULL when no rule fired and the default stood.

schema.name: section_diffs
schema.description: One row per compared pair of consecutive printings of one bill. `engine_name`, `engine_version` and `engine_revision` record which diff engine produced the row.

properties.name: bill_id
properties.description: The bill both printings belong to.

properties.name: from_version_code
properties.description: The earlier printing's version code.

properties.name: from_printing_id
properties.description: Which acquisition path supplied the earlier printing.

properties.name: to_version_code
properties.description: The later printing's version code.

properties.name: to_printing_id
properties.description: Which acquisition path supplied the later printing.

properties.name: from_version_date
properties.description: The earlier printing's publisher date.

properties.name: to_version_date
properties.description: The later printing's publisher date; the merge prefers the larger value.

properties.name: added_count
properties.description: Sections present only in the later printing.

properties.name: removed_count
properties.description: Sections present only in the earlier printing.

properties.name: modified_count
properties.description: Sections present in both whose body text differs.

properties.name: unchanged_count
properties.description: Sections present in both whose body text is identical.

properties.name: moved_count
properties.description: Sections the move round paired at a different path.

properties.name: item_count
properties.description: How many section_diff_items rows this diff produced.

schema.dataGranularityDescription: One row per compared pair of consecutive printings of one bill.
